item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Sat Nov 14, 8:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt

item.title: UC Davis Arboretum Clearance Plant Sale — Sat Nov 14, 9:00 AM — Arboretum Teaching Nursery
item.description:

All plants will be marked down 20%, and Friends members save an additional 10%. Help us celebrate the UC Davis Arboretum and Public Garden’s 90th anniversary while finding a few new favorites for your garden or home. item.title: Tree Davis Planting Event at Toad Hollow Dog Park — Sat Nov 14, 9:00 AM — Toad Hollow
item.description:
Help us plant trees in the Toad Hollow dog park! We will be digging tree holes, planting trees, and installing support stakes. We will be meeting at 1919 2nd St. Overflow parking is available along 2nd St. Please reach out to info@treedavis.org if you would like to sign up with a group of 10 volunteers or more. If you do not reach out, we will not hold your reservation. Safety – All volunteers must bring their own water, snacks, sun protection, and wear closed toed shoes. We request that volunteers who are feeling ill in any form wait until they are fully recovered to participate in Tree Davis events.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Layered Beginnings: An Abstraction by Design Workshop with Michael Shemchuk — Sat Nov 14, 10:00 AM — Pence Gallery
item.description:
Layered Beginnings: An Abstraction by Design Workshop with Michael Shemchuk Saturday & Sunday, November 14-15 | 10 AM – 4:30 PM $320 Members, $350 Non-Members (Materials not included) This mixed media workshop tackles creating dynamic, textured surfaces as a first step in the Abstraction by Design process. Under the guidance of artist Michael Shemchuk, participants will apply layers of paper and paint and produce surfaces that enable them to sand, scrape, peel, paint, collage and repeat multiple times. During this workshop, students will complete a series of layered surfaces, which are ideal for furthering paint & collage projects. Please note that some prep assignments will need to be completed before the workshop starts. See the materials list on our website for more information. Register here: https://pencegallery.org/education/programs/workshops-and-classes/ Any questions? Email pencegallery@gmail.com.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Together Again, 1960–2026: Perspectives from UC Davis' Fine Arts Collection — Sat Nov 14, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description:
This ongoing collection exhibition traces a history of art forged from this place. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, “Together Again” proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: The HIVE Anniversary Party — Sat Nov 14, 11:00 AM — The HIVE Tasting Room and Kitchen
item.description:
Celebrate The HIVE’s 5th anniversary and Z Specialty Food’s 47th during this FREE community event. Kick off your holiday shopping, taste 30+ varietal honeys, craft mead and enjoy selections from our farm-to-fork menu. This over the top celebration features live music from Wolf Jett, steep holiday discounts, giveaways and interactive activities for all ages including honey and mead tastings, honey bee education with live bees, tours of our pollinator garden and facility, a HIVE Spelling Bee and Waggle Dance Competition. In honor of 47 years of business and The HIVE’s 5th year, we’re offering a $20 Gift Card with each $100 retail purchase in the warehouse. The HIVE, a vibrant community gathering space, is home to Moon Shine Trading Co. and Island of the Moon Honey, visionaries of varietal honey since 1979.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Above Bone — Sat Nov 14, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: ADERO WILLARD ABOVE BONE November 6–29, 2026 Reception and Artist Talk on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM Artist in the gallery on Sundays, November 8 and 29, 12–5 PM Axis Gallery presents Above Bone, an exhibition of ceramic sculpture by Sacramento artist Adero Willard, on view November 6 through 29, 2026. The exhibition brings together new work and pieces never before shown in Sacramento or on the West Coast. Join the artist for the reception and artist talk on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM. ABOUT THE EXHIBITION Above Bone refers to what is beneath, the layers, and what emerges. Clay sculptural vessels of heads and body forms explore death, regeneration, new growth, and what is hidden. Adero wrestles clay into expressive forms and creates surfaces dense in color and pattern: thick clay and delicately etched vines and flowers. The forms are camouflaged, as if growing from or being returned to the ground. Layered colorful patterns, resists, and luster build up over multiple firings. Pat

item.title: Capturing Memories of Grief/Capturando Memorias del Duelo — Sat Nov 14, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: SUMMER VENTIS AND LINA RINCÓN CAPTURING MEMORIES OF GRIEF/CAPTURANDO MEMORIAS DEL DUELO November 6–29, 2026 Reception on Saturday, November 7, 5–8 PM The project, “Capturing Memories of Grief,” is a collaboration between artist Summer Ventis, sociologist and poet Lina Rincón, and you. Together, we explore the intersection of grief, memory, and image. We began this project with a conversation about our shared experience of losing a parent. When we recalled these experiences, we learned that we both had memories that centered around images, photographs, and the process of photography as a way to make sense of and process the meanings of our loss. In Fall of 2025, we began a series of grief-themed tours of works in the Crocker Art Museum’s collection. At the end of the tours, participants gathered to share and document our memories of grief and loss and how they connect with different types of images. item.title: The Lion King Jr — Sat Nov 14, 2:00 PM — Davis Musical Theatre Co. (DMTC)
item.description:
November 14 through December 13, 2026 The Lion King is the story of Simba, an adventurous and energetic lion cub who is next in line to be king of the Pride Lands, a thriving and beautiful region in the African savanna. When Simba’s father Mufasa is killed by his uncle Scar, though, Simba is led to believe that his father’s death is his fault, and he is encouraged to run away forever. Scar seizes power and with his already unstable mind deteriorating, the Pride Lands experiences a darkness and desolation from which only Simba can save the animals of the kingdom. Featuring classic songs from the film such as “Circle of Life,” “I Just Can’t Wait to Be King,” “Hakuna Matata,” and “Can You Feel the Love Tonight,” The Lion King is a story and a spectacle about identity, family, and responsibility that is enjoyed worldwide by people of all ages. Recommended for all ages
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Pamela Trokanski Dance Theatre 2026 Fall Concert - Walking Contradictions — Sat Nov 14, 6:00 PM — Louise H Kellogg Memorial Theater at the Pamela Trokanski Dance Workshop
item.description:
The Pamela Trokanski Dance Theatre invites the community to join them for the premiere of their Fall Concert: Walking Contradictions, a thoughtful, and sometimes humorous exploration of our lives as asymmetrical beings, finding beauty in the balance of symmetry but at the same time seemingly unable to escape what is unbalanced, whether that is in ourselves, our communities, or in how we behave in the world around us. Joining the PTDT are the PTDT Apprentice Company, Light Ballet Company, and The Third Stage. Known for work that integrates a strong sense of athleticism and technical training with idiosyncratic movements and a diverse range of movers, including dancers ranging in age from 10 to 90+, this is not your average dance performance! Tickets are available in advance and at the door. General Admission – $20 Children, Students, and Adults 65+ – $15 (A 4% surcharge is added to all electronic payments)
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Yoga & Sound Immersion (Davis) — Sat Dec 12, 3:30 PM — Blanchard Room
item.description:
Join us for a 45 min Vinyasa yoga class followed by a 45min Sound Immersion (Sound Bath) session that will leave you feeling refreshed and grounded. Yoga will help you ease into the practice and find clam. The sound immersion combines breathwork, light stretching, and a sound bath with crystal singing bowls, chimes, bells, wave drum, and rain sticks.
All levels welcome. Please dress comfortably and bring a yoga mat or something comfortable to lie on.
Source: Yolo Library

item.title: Manetti Shrem Museum: Together Again, 1960–2026, Perspectives from UC Davis’ Fine Arts Collection — Thu Nov 26, 10:00 AM — Jan Shrem and Maria Manetti Shrem Museum of Art at UC Davis
item.description: Together Again inaugurates the Manetti Shrem Museum’s ongoing collection galleries. This exhibition highlighting the collection will be on long-term view, accompanied by temporary exhibitions each fall and winter. The ongoing collection galleries trace a history of art forged from UC Davis and throughout Northern California. By focusing on relationships of many kinds, this presentation proposes that in order to understand an artwork in all its fullness, chance encounters and long-standing friendships often matter as much as formal affiliations. UC Davis legends such as Wayne Thiebaud, Deborah Butterfield and Bruce Nauman are exhibited alongside important regional voices that were once overlooked, and the exhibition extends to the artists shaping Northern California today, including Sadie Barnette, Woody De Othello and Ruby Neri. Together Again builds bridges between who we were and who we are becoming at UC Davis, and affirms the Manetti Shrem Museum as home to the complex story of No

item.title: Human Relations Commission Meetings — Thu Nov 26, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July).
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site.
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council.
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Jan 27, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.
You're not required to buy anything in order to join us, but we do encourage you to support local businesses. Blue Note's chef team makes a mean pizza, and there are other nearby downtown restaurants
